items.summary: حملات حوثی‌های یمن به عربستان سعودی ادامه دارد و فرودگاه بین‌المللی ریاض برای سومین بار در چهار روز هدف قرار گرفته است. مقام‌های سعودی از افزایش شمار مجروحان خبر داده‌اند. در حمله روز شنبه به این فرودگاه ۱۳ نفر کشته شدند. فرودگاه دمام نیز هدف حمله قرار گرفته و یک پهپاد در شرق عربستان رهگیری شده است. حوثی‌ها به شرکت‌های هواپیمایی و مسافران درباره استفاده از فرودگاه‌ها و حریم هوایی عربستان هشدار داده‌اند.

items.summary: یکی از بازماندگان قتل عام فورت هود در سال 2009 می‌گوید که آرزو می‌کند تیرانداز دسته‌جمعی به ازای هر زندگی که در آن روز گرفته، یک بار کشته شود - اما حتی او تصمیم ارتش را برای پخش زنده مرگ او زیر سوال می‌برد. نیدال حسن، 56 ساله، قرار است در 3 دسامبر 2026 با جوخه تیرباران اعدام شود، و وزیر جنگ پیت هگست h اوایل این ماه اعلام کرد که این جوخه برای پخش عمومی در دسترس خواهد بود. "چرا مردم می خواهند آن را ببینند؟" جولیا ویلسون، کارمند غیرنظامی سابق وزارت دفاع که 17 سال پیش از تیراندازی جان سالم به در برد، به فاکس نیوز دیجیتال گفت. ویلسون می خواهد تیرانداز دسته جمعی اعدام شود، و به عنوان یک قربانی، او می خواهد در اعدام او شرکت کند و به چشمان او نگاه کند. حسن، یک روانپزشک ارتش در آن زمان، در 5 نوامبر 2009 وارد یک مرکز آمادگی سرباز در تگزاس A شد.
items.summary_original: A survivor of the 2009 Fort Hood massacre says she wishes the mass shooter could be killed one time for every life he took that day – but even she is questioning the military's decision to livestream his death. Nidal Hasan, 56, is scheduled to face execution by firing squad on Dec. 3, 2026, and Secretary of War Pete Hegset h announced earlier this month that it will be made available to stream to the public. "Why would people want to see that?" Julia Wilson, a former Defense Department civilian employee who survived the shooting 17 years ago, told Fox News Digital. Wilson wants the mass shooter executed, and, as a victim, she wants to attend his execution and look him in the eye. Hasan, an Army psychiatrist at the time, walked into a soldier readiness center on Nov. 5, 2009, on the Texas Army post and opened fire, killing 13 people and wounding 32 others. Following a military court-martial verdict, Hasan was sentenced to death on Aug. 28, 2013. FORT HOOD SURVIVOR SHOT IN HEAD VOWS TO WATCH TERRORIST FACE HISTORIC FIRING SQUAD On Oct. 2, President Donald Trump approved the death sentence, and days later Hegseth announced it would be by a public firing squad. "Personally, I do want to be there," Wilson told Fox News Digital. "I do want to look him in the eye to let him know, ‘Look, I may have been your victim that day, but I'm not your victim anymore. I survived you. My child survived you, a lot of us survived you. You didn't do as much damage as you thought you were going to.'

items.title_original: British adventurer returns home after 28-year walk around the world
items.summary: کارل بوشبی، ماجراجو، سرانجام پس از 28 سال سفر در سراسر جهان، پا به خاک بریتانیا گذاشت. در 5 اکتبر، او اعلام کرد که کانال مانش را از فرانسه به انگلستان شنا کرده است. در حالی که در دوور استراحت می کرد، گفت: "من به یونیون جک که بیرون از این هتل در حال پرواز است خیره شده ام. در طول روزها پرچم های زیادی دیده ام، اما آن یکی خاص است." او در رسانه های اجتماعی یکی از اولین وعده های غذایی خود را به اشتراک گذاشت، در حالی که از خوردن دوباره ماهی و چیپس بریتانیایی بسیار خوشحال بود. دیل «ریش خاکستری» سندرز عنوان مسن‌ترین فرد برای راهپیمایی در مسیر آپالاچیان در 91 سالگی را پس می‌گیرد سفر او هنوز به پایان نرسیده است. او امیدوار است تا پایان ماه به خط پایان برسد - خانه مادرش در هال. به گفته وب سایت او، او در دهه 1990 کارت تولدی از پدرش دریافت کرد که در مورد دو سرباز که بر سر یک شاهکار غیرممکن دعوا می کردند.
items.summary_original: Adventurer Karl Bushby has finally stepped foot on UK soil after a 28-year journey across the world. On Oct. 5, he announced he swam the English Channel , from France to England. While resting in Dover, he said, "I’m staring at the Union Jack flying outside this hotel. I’ve seen many flags over the days, but that one is special." On social media he shared one of his first meals back, overjoyed to have authentic British fish and chips again. DALE 'GREY BEARD' SANDERS RECLAIMS TITLE AS OLDEST PERSON TO THRU-HIKE THE APPALACHIAN TRAIL AT 91 His journey is not over yet. He hopes to reach the finish line — his mother’s home in Hull — by the end of the month. According to his website , he received a birthday card in the 1990s from his father about two soldiers arguing over an impossible feat, walking from London to New York via the Bering Strait. Karl grabbed a map and drew a single line, knowing he found his life’s mission. NAVY VETERANS REUNITE AFTER 30 YEARS FOR 'GRUELING' CROSS-COUNTRY BIKE CHALLENGE HONORING 9/11 On Nov. 1, 1998, the ex-paratrooper started his journey in Chile, with only a few hundred dollars in his pocket "South America, you were young, it was all new, it was the boys adventure dream," Bushby said. He walked north to the United States, waiting for the Bering Strait to freeze to cross from Alaska into Russia. In April 2012, Russia denied his next visa, pausing his expedition. items.summary: یک قاضی فدرال منصوب بایدن که قبلاً شکایتی رسمی از وزارت دادگستری دونالد ترامپ، رئیس جمهور آمریکا به دلیل تعصب ادعا کرده بود، بار دیگر در روز دوشنبه در یک رویارویی شدید بر سر برداشتن سریع درختان در یک زمین گلف تاریخی در پارک ملی، در میان وکلای دولت فوران کرد. قاضی آنا ریس آخرین سرزنش خود را در جریان یک جلسه استماع اضطراری در مورد صدها درخت برداشته شده از لینک های گلف ایست پوتوماک در هاینز پوینت دی سی بیان کرد. ترامپ می خواهد این مرکز عمومی تاریخی را به یک زمین گلف با کالیبر قهرمانی مانند زمین های خود در ایالات متحده، ایرلند و اسکاتلند تبدیل کند - آخرین برخورد دولت دادگاه با مخالفان سیاسی. اسکات مک فارلین، روزنامه‌نگار، که از جلسه استماع به صورت زنده توییت کرد، ریس را به عنوان «فریاد» در مقابل وکلای دولت توصیف کرد.
items.summary_original: A Biden-appointed federal judge who previously drew a formal misconduct complaint from President Donald Trump's Justice Department for alleged bias erupted at government lawyers again Monday, in a heated showdown over rapid tree removal at a historic golf course on national parkland. Judge Ana Reyes unleashed her latest rebuke during an emergency hearing over hundreds of trees removed from East Potomac Golf Links in Hains Point, D.C. Trump wants to transform the historic public facility into a championship-caliber golf course like his courses in the U.S., Ireland and Scotland – the latest courtroom collision between the administration and its political opponents. Journalist Scott MacFarlane, who live-tweeted from the hearing, described Reyes as "scream[ing]" at administration attorneys over the government's late-Friday notification that tree removal would begin Saturday. A government lawyer acknowledged that approximately 430 trees had already been cut down, according to MacFarlane. OBAMA-APPOINTED JUDGE TORCHES TRUMP ADMIN IN LATEST COURTROOM SHOWDOWN, REFERS ATTORNEY FOR BAR REVIEW "You've lost credibility!" Reyes told government attorneys, according to MacFarlane's live courtroom reporting. The administration maintains that the removals implement a 2019 National Park Service landscape-restoration plan predating Trump's redesign proposal for the links, which sit on an island connected to the city proper by the Jefferson Memorial and Francis Case Bridge at its western edge.

items.summary_original: With just over three weeks to go until Election Day , more and more red states and congressional districts appear in reach for the Democrats, as they work to win back House and Senate majorities from the Republicans in the midterms. But a massive Republican spending advantage threatens to complicate those ambitions. Republican campaigns, committees and aligned groups have outspent their Democratic counterparts by $400 million so far this election cycle, according to AdImpact, a leading political advertising tracking firm. The disparity is forcing Democrats to make difficult decisions about where to invest and how much to spend as the party tries to expand the electoral map . "We are being outspent by the Republicans. That's just a fact," Lauren French, communications director at the Senate Majority PAC, told Fox News Digital. "In many of these states, they have really transactionalized elections, so they have monopoly money to play with, whereas we are working with real resources." The Senate showdown in reliably Republican Kansas is Lean Republican, while the races in red-leaning Alaska, Iowa, Ohio and Texas are rated toss-ups. items.summary: در یکی از شدیدترین رقابت‌های انتخاباتی فرمانداری در کشور، نامزد دموکرات برای ایجاد چهره‌ای معتدل کار می‌کرده است – در حالی که طبق گزارش‌ها در کلیسایی حضور می‌یابد که آشکارا برخی از دلایل مترقی را که بین رای‌دهندگان در آیووا ایجاد تفرقه می‌کنند، می‌پذیرد. به گفته یک روزنامه نگار محلی، راب سند، حسابرس ایالت آیووا و نامزد دموکرات آن برای فرمانداری، از اواخر سال 2025 به طور منظم در کلیسای متحد مسیحی جماعت پلیموث، واقع در پایتخت این ایالت، شرکت می کرد. در طول سال‌ها، پلیموث اجراهای درگ کوئین را میزبانی و تبلیغ کرده است، از یک کشیش تراجنسیتی دعوت کرده تا به عنوان کشیش مهمان خدمت کند و آشکارا از سقط جنین حمایت کرده است. سند بر ایمان خود در مسیر مبارزات انتخاباتی تأکید کرده است، و مکرراً به مسیحیت اشاره می کند و از کتاب مقدس استناد می کند، و در مواقعی با موفقیت به موارد دیگر متوسل می شود.
items.summary_original: In one of the most hotly contested governor's races in the country, the Democratic nominee has been working overtime to cultivate a moderate image — while reportedly attending a church that openly embraces some of the progressive causes dividing voters in Iowa. Rob Sand, Iowa’s state auditor and its Democratic nominee for governor, regularly attended Plymouth Congregational United Church of Christ, located in the state’s capital, as of late 2025, according to a local journalist. Over the years, Plymouth has hosted and promoted drag queen performances, invited a transgender pastor to serve as a guest pastor and openly supported abortion. Sand has emphasized his faith on the campaign trail, repeatedly referencing Christianity and quoting scripture, at times successfully appealing to otherwise conservative Iowans. In addition to leaning on his faith, Sand has repeatedly described himself as independently minded, claimed to have voted for Republicans in the past and said that he sometimes prefers working with the GOP over Democrats, calling political parties "poison." "I am a Christian. I’m a conservative. But I’m not a party-based person," one voter is quoted as saying in a Sand press release. "I like to vote for the person as opposed to the party. And to me, (Sand) just seems really honest and down to earth. And I enjoyed him." items.summary_original: A wealthy Southern enclave once known as a playground for retirees and snowbirds is transforming into a growing technology and financial hub, drawing comparisons to Silicon Valley as businesses, Wall Street executives and entrepreneurs move in. Palm Beach County, Florida, is attracting new attention as wealthy Americans seek alternatives to high-tax states like New York and California. "Palm Beach has changed from a place where people come to retire to a place that people come to build," luxury real estate expert Margit Brandt told Fox News Digital. "There's been countless CEOs and major heads of companies that have moved their businesses to Palm Beach," she said, pointing to Florida's favorable tax climate and lifestyle as major draws. THE RED STATES RACING AHEAD IN AMERICA’S POWERFUL WEALTH BOOM — AND THE STATES FALLING BEHIND The region is also home to President Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago estate, often dubbed the "Southern White House," placing the emerging business hub in the backyard of one of the country's most recognizable political landmarks. The shift comes amid changing migration patterns across the country, with Internal Revenue Service data for 2022–2023 showing taxpayer losses across numerous California and Northeastern counties , while much of the Southeast recorded gains. items.summary_original: As lawmakers spar over whether to expand the U.S. Supreme Court beyond nine justices, Americans interviewed by Fox News Digital on Capitol Hill had competing views on whether the nation's highest court needs a shake-up at all. "If it's not broken, don't fix it," Tim from Washington, D.C. , told Fox News Digital. "If you had more justices, you could have more differing opinions there," Derek, also from Washington, said. "So you'd have to have more of a consensus on whatever they're voting on." The debate comes after a Republican-backed constitutional amendment to permanently fix the court at nine justices failed in the House in September, falling short of the two-thirds majority required for passage. MORNING GLORY: DSA DEMOCRATS' RADICAL PLAN TO RESHAPE AMERICA STARTS WITH THE SUPREME COURT Democratic lawmakers have also introduced proposals to reshape the court, including legislation to expand its membership, establish term limits and impose additional ethics requirements. " If we're gonna change the size, we need to do it now," said Carl from Texas. "If you're going to pack the court, let's pack it now." One person Fox News Digital spoke with questioned the motives behind efforts to increase the number of justices. "I think those who want to increase the size, maybe just have a bias to it, if it be Republican or Democrat," Tim said about the idea of expanding the number of justices. items.summary_original: Sen. Roger Marshall , R-Kan., paid a six-year-old campaign bill after a bakery owner called him out on social media for allegedly failing to pay for cookies and other treats ordered for a 2020 election watch party. Holly Thomas, a bakery founder, said in an Oct. 8 Facebook post that she would never vote for Marshall because his campaign had failed to pay a $678.75 bill despite her repeated attempts to collect the money. Thomas shared an image of the invoice and a photo that appeared to show custom cookies made for Marshall's campaign. "Do you know why I will never vote for Roger Marshall? Because six years ago, when I was a brand-new small business owner, his campaign ordered cookies and treats from my bakery for his primary election watch party. And I never got paid. For nearly a year, I made repeated attempts to collect payment, reaching out by phone and email. I never received a return phone call, and the invoice was never paid," Thomas wrote in the post. SLEEPER SENATE RACE EMERGES AS UNEXPECTED HEADACHE FOR REPUBLICANS AHEAD OF MIDTERMS "Not only was I just starting out, but we were also in the middle of COVID, when small businesses everywhere were struggling just to keep their doors open. Every single dollar mattered. Those cookies and treats cost money to make, employees' time to prepare, and resources that my little business couldn't afford to give away," she explained. "Six years later, I haven't forgotten. This isn't about political parties or policy disagreements.

items.summary_original: LOS ANGELES — Surrounded by sprawling homeless encampments, drug use and trash-strewn sidewalks in the heart of Los Angeles' Skid Row, Republican gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton blasted California's homelessness crisis as a "political scandal," accusing Democratic leaders of spending billions in taxpayer dollars while allowing the streets to deteriorate. "'The homelessness crisis,' as if it's some kind of natural disaster that can't be helped," Hilton told Fox News Digital, referring to how politicians and others describe the conditions as he surveyed the sprawling encampments. "No, it is not a crisis. It's actually a scandal. It's a political scandal because the people in charge, they've caused this with their policies." Skid Row, the epicenter of California's homelessness crisis, is facing renewed scrutiny after a sweeping federal drug raid Thursday. The crackdown came as voting gets underway in the Nov. 3 governor's race, with Hilton challenging Democrat Xavier Becerra in a contest where homelessness and billions in taxpayer spending have emerged, yet again, as key campaign issues. items.summary_original: Republicans are gaining ground in blue-leaning Oregon, where Fox News Power Rankings have shifted the governor's race toward the GOP as Democratic Gov. Tina Kotek faces a competitive rematch with Republican Christine Drazan. The shift from Likely Democrat to Lean Democrat reflects a competitive political environment in Oregon, where concerns over homelessness, housing, taxes, schools and the cost of living have created an opening for Republicans to end a more than four-decade losing streak in gubernatorial elections. Republicans are gaining ground in Oregon even as they face a rough national political environment marked by high gas and diesel prices, what polls show is an unpopular war in Iran and President Donald Trump's low approval ratings. "This is something historic we're trying to pull off," Drazan said in a Fox News Digital interview. "It's been a long time, and we're due we win." Ron Wyden won his 2022 re-election by 15 points. But gubernatorial showdowns in the northwestern state have traditionally been much closer contests. Drazan, a former GOP leader in the Oregon House, lost to Kotek by less than four points in 2022. items.summary_original: Pope Leo XIV condemned the death penalty as "inadmissible" as the Pentagon faces criticism over plans to livestream an execution later this year. Leo, the first American pope, shared his opposition to capital punishment Saturday in a social media post marking World Day Against the Death Penalty. Citing Catholic doctrine revised under his predecessor, Pope Francis, Leo emphasized that the death penalty violates human dignity. "The death penalty is inadmissible because it is an attack on the inviolability and dignity of the person. The common good can be safeguarded and the requirements of justice can be met without recourse to capital punishment: effective systems of detention have been developed that protect citizens while at the same time do not completely deprive those who are guilty of the possibility of redemption," Leo wrote on X. "#NoDeathPenalty," he added in the post. VETERAN SHOT 7 TIMES IN FORT HOOD MASSACRE HAS A WARNING FOR AMERICANS PLANNING TO WATCH EXECUTION In 2018, Francis revised the Catholic Church's official position on capital punishment, declaring the death penalty "inadmissible" in all circumstances. "Consequently the church teaches, in the light of the Gospel, that the death penalty is inadmissible because it is an attack on the inviolability and dignity of the person," the revised Catechism states. items.summary_original: At least 139 migrants, including 15 children, died when a boat carrying more than 300 people capsized off the coast of Djibouti, according to the United Nations' migration agency. The vessel was carrying 305 people from Djibouti toward Yemen when it capsized Thursday night or early Friday near Guhere, north of Obock, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) said Sunday. At least 84 people remained missing as of Sunday, while more than 80 survived. All the survivors were Ethiopian nationals , according to the agency. "No one gets into a boat like that unless they believe there is no other safe way," IOM Director General Amy Pope said in a statement. I am asking governments and donors to act before the next boat goes down," Pope added. The confirmed death toll includes only victims buried by authorities in Djibouti and could rise as additional bodies are verified, IOM Chief of Mission in Djibouti Alexandre Coissac told The Associated Press. items.summary_original: Iran-backed Houthis launched a series of attacks on Saudi Arabian airports through Sunday, reportedly killing at least 14 people, including an American, and injuring more than 300 others, according to reports . The attacks heightened fears of a wider Middle East war as regional experts warned of "cross-domain escalation" amid heightened tensions over Washington's September actions against Iran's aviation sector. The Houthis claimed responsibility for earlier attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, while U.S. officials blamed the Iran-backed group for Saturday's strike, which reportedly killed 13 people and injured more than 300. SAUDI FOREIGN MINISTER WARNS HOUTHI THREAT GOES GLOBAL AS TRUMP HOLDS FIRE Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said another attack on Sunday killed a Pakistani resident and injured 11 others. Meanwhile, an airport in Dammam, in the kingdom's Eastern Province, was also reportedly targeted by the Houthis. "Cross-domain escalation by Iran and its proxies will continue to be a primary strategy," Behnam Ben Taleblu , senior director of the Iran Program and a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told Fox News Digital on Sunday. "The emphasis on aviation targets connects directly to the closing of Iran's aviation sector and sanctions imposed on its commercial airlines under the U.S. maximum pressure campaign," he warned. items.summary: کیمبرلی گیلفویل، سفیر ایالات متحده در یونان ممکن است به زودی برکنار شود، زیرا گزارش هایی وجود دارد که او به دنبال کمک مالی شش رقمی کارت اعتباری از یک اهدا کننده ترامپ بوده و در عین حال امکان دسترسی به مقامات دولت را فراهم کرده است، و این به اتهامات فزاینده در مورد رفتار او در آتن افزوده است. آسوشیتدپرس روز یکشنبه به نقل از یک مقام ارشد آمریکایی گزارش داد که دونالد ترامپ، رئیس جمهور آمریکا و مارکو روبیو، وزیر امور خارجه، از رفتار گزارش شده گیلفویل "به شدت عصبانی" هستند و در حال بررسی برکناری او هستند. این مقام به AP گفت که تصمیم در مورد اقداماتی که باید انجام شود احتمالاً این هفته پس از تعطیلات روز کلمبوس در روز دوشنبه گرفته خواهد شد. هیچ خروجی تایید نشده است. گیلفویل، نامزد سابق دونالد ترامپ جونیور، این هفته پس از آنکه وال استریت ژورنال گزارش داد که از اریک دیترز، اهداکننده ترامپ خواسته است 100 دلار را بپردازد، مورد بررسی قرار گرفت.

President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are "extremely pissed off" by Guilfoyle’s reported conduct and are weighing her removal, The Associated Press reported Sunday, citing a senior U.S. official. The official told the AP that a decision on what action to take would likely come this week after Monday’s Columbus Day holiday. No departure has been confirmed. Guilfoyle, onetime fiancée of Donald Trump Jr., came under scrutiny this week after The Wall Street Journal reported that she asked Trump donor Eric Deters to pay off a $100,000 American Express bill shortly before her Senate confirmation hearing. Deters said he never made the payment. Guilfoyle’s attorneys, Jesse Binnall and David M. items.summary_original: President Donald Trump's efforts to reach a diesel agreement with Russia could provide Russian President Vladimir Putin with fresh revenue to fund his war against Ukraine while allowing Moscow to buy time through negotiations it has little intention of honoring, a former NATO commander warned Sunday. Retired Gen. Philip Breedlove , former NATO supreme allied commander Europe and head of U.S. European Command, told Fox News Digital that Washington also risks undermining Ukraine's war effort by striking a deal with what he called "the enemy." "And so we are cutting a deal with the enemy," Breedlove said, warning that "all of this money will go into fueling Mr. Putin's continued attacks in Ukraine." The Russian government said Saturday it had partially lifted a ban on diesel exports with immediate effect, following the new agreement between Putin and Trump for Russia to supply the U.S. and global markets, Reuters reported. As previously reported by Fox News Digital, Trump's package calls for the release of 300,000 tonnes of diesel "to the American and global marketplace," followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and another 1 million tonnes afterward. items.summary: واشنگتن دی سی – آخر این هفته، میلیون‌ها فعال ضد اسرائیلی در خیابان‌های شهرها در اقدامات هماهنگ از پایتخت آمریکا تا لندن، پاریس، مادرید و کوالالامپار مالزی راهپیمایی کردند و شعارهای آشنای «فلسطین آزاد، آزاد» و «از رودخانه تا دریا، فلسطین آزاد خواهد شد» را سر دادند. اما برای اولین بار که در مصاحبه های اختصاصی با فاکس نیوز دیجیتال به صراحت صحبت شد، سه رهبر ضد اسرائیلی هدف را تصدیق کردند: یک کشور به نام «فلسطین» شامل اسرائیل امروزی، کرانه باختری و غزه، با «حق بازگشت» فلسطینی ها به کشور جدید و حقوق مساوی سیاسی، رای و شهروندی برای یهودیانی که در حال حاضر در کنار اسرائیل زندگی می کنند. مهمتر از همه، در بینش سیاسی که آنها توصیف کردند، اسرائیل به طور قانونی این کار را متوقف خواهد کرد

But for the first time, communicated frankly in exclusive interviews with Fox News Digital, three anti-Israel leaders acknowledged the goal: one state called "Palestine" encompassing modern-day Israel, the West Bank and Gaza, with a Palestinian "right of return" to the new country and equal political, voting and citizenship rights for Palestinians alongside Jews currently living in Israel. Most significantly, in the political vision they described, Israel would legally cease to exist as a separate Jewish nation-state and Jews would be quickly overwhelmed demographically. There are another estimated 10.2 million Jews worldwide. There are about 5.5 million Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza and about 8 million Palestinians in the diaspora, totaling about 13.5 million. items.summary_original: Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei claimed Oct. 8 that U.S. and Israeli strikes had failed to undermine Iran's domestic security forces, praising police personnel for resisting attacks launched in February under Operations Epic Fury and Roaring Lion. Khamenei's remarks on X also came as the U.S. Army released a new battlefield identification guide to help American troops recognize members of Iran's conventional military, known as the Artesh, whose ground forces were estimated by the Jerusalem Institute for Strategy and Security in June at 350,000 personnel. "The criminal US-Zionist enemy's desperate efforts and malicious attacks on the pillars of social order and security, which are unparalleled throughout history, have not caused the courageous personnel of the Police Force to waver even a fraction in their mission," Khamenei wrote in a statement. Khamenei specifically praised Iran's Law Enforcement Command, known as FARAJA, accusing the United States and Israel of targeting the institution responsible for maintaining domestic order. "The focus and persistence of the criminal US-Zionist enemy in striking at the Police Force at its various levels, from its highest command levels down to those who are on the frontline, has only served to underscore the paramount importance of this institution more than ever," he wrote. items.summary: جوامع در حال ارزیابی خسارات ناشی از طوفان قدرتمندی هستند که منطقه را درنوردید، خانه‌ها را آسیب دید، جاده‌ها را زیر آب گرفت و محله‌ها را پر از آوار کرد. عکس‌های برخی از مناطقی که بیشترین آسیب را دیده‌اند، میزان تخریب را نشان می‌دهد، زیرا ساکنان و خدمه اورژانس روند طولانی پاکسازی و بازسازی را آغاز می‌کنند. چگونه طوفان رده 2 خشونت آمیز در سراسر فلوریدا و ساحل خلیج فارس در روز جمعه، 9 اکتبر، به عنوان یک طوفان رده 2 با حداکثر بادهای پایدار با سرعت 105 مایل در ساعت، به پانهندل فلوریدا در نزدیکی Destin برخورد کرد، و بادهای مخربی را به همراه داشت. طوفان سقف ساختمان ها را پاره کرد، درختان را ریشه کن کرد و برق صدها هزار مشتری را در فلوریدا و آلاباما قطع کرد.
items.summary_original: Communities are beginning to assess the damage left behind by a powerful hurricane that tore through the region, leaving homes damaged, roads flooded and neighborhoods littered with debris. Photos from some of the hardest-hit areas show the scale of the destruction as residents and emergency crews begin the long process of cleaning up and rebuilding. HOW THE VIOLENT CATEGORY 2 STORM UNFOLDED ACROSS FLORIDA AND GULF COAST Isaias slammed into the Florida Panhandle near Destin on Friday, Oct. 9, as a Category 2 hurricane with maximum sustained winds of 105 mph, bringing destructive winds, dangerous storm surge and widespread flooding. The hurricane tore roofs from buildings, uprooted trees and knocked out power to hundreds of thousands of customers across Florida and Alabama before pushing inland. STUNNING FOOTAGE CAPTURES HURRICANE ISAIAS FROM INSIDE THE STORM’S EYE Isaias marked the first hurricane to make landfall along the U.S. Gulf Coast since Hurricane Milton battered Florida in October 2024, nearly two years earlier. The storm also became the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic season, ending an unusually quiet stretch that saw no hurricanes develop until October. DESANTIS DEPLOYS AN ARMY TO CLEAR ROADS, RESTORE POWER AFTER ISAIAS' LANDFALL As Isaias moved inland and weakened, the full extent of the hurricane's destruction began to emerge. Stunning images from across the Gulf Coast capture what the powerful storm left behind.

items.summary_original: The FlyDubai attempted hijacking shows the U.S. and its allies are still using outdated counterterrorism assumptions against increasingly sophisticated enemies, a U.S. rescue expert and 9/11 first responder warns. "They’re good at chess," Bryan Stern, chairman and CEO of Grey Bull Rescue, told Fox News Digital on Monday, saying the radical ideology behind the FlyDubai attack is a ringing "bell" for global aviation security and Western counterterrorism strategy. "And we’re, if we’re lucky, playing checkers – if we’re lucky – and I would argue we’re not even playing checkers that well." TERROR CELLS INSIDE FOREIGN AIRLINES 'CERTAINLY A POSSIBILITY,' RETIRED PILOT WARNS Stern, whose global nonprofit conducts evacuations from war zones and hostage situations, said the thwarted FlyDubai attack by "an angry, radicalized, Sunni bad guy" is showing just how far behind our enemies we are in this post-9/11 world. "They understand us significantly more than we understand them," Stern, who has been "hunting the bad guys" for 30 years, said. Stern said the U.S. has to understand the "asymmetric warfare" as well as the increasingly sophisticated enemy does. "The reason why a football coach watches game tapes is not to watch his own team play, it's to watch the bad guys play," he said. "We gotta start watching some game tapes." items.summary_original: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is coordinating with federal agencies to monitor travelers entering the United States from Siberia amid concerns about a possible pneumonic plague outbreak in Russia, the agency's director revealed Wednesday. CDC Director Dr. Erica Schwartz said the Trump administration is working across multiple agencies to identify travelers arriving from the region following the mysterious death of a Russian laboratory worker, while emphasizing that the risk to Americans remains minimal. "We are very confident that the threat to the United States is extremely low," Schwartz said during a Wall Street Journal health forum Wednesday. MOTHER OF DEAD RUSSIAN ANTI-PLAGUE INSTITUTE WORKER: 'I KNOW THE TRUTH' The concerns stem from the Oct. 2 death of Darya Shipilova, a 28-year-old employee of the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute in Siberia, whose death has fueled speculation about a possible pneumonic plague infection . Russian authorities have maintained that Shipilova died from pneumonia of unknown origin and have not confirmed that she was infected with Yersinia pestis, the bacteria that causes pneumonic plague. Schwartz said the CDC is working with the departments of Homeland Security, State and War, among other federal agencies, to track potential arrivals from the region. "در جنگ بین روسیه و اوکراین آتش بس انرژی برقرار می شود. هر دو طرف توافق کرده اند. آن را نشکنید!" ترامپ در Truth Social نوشت. این اعلامیه در حالی صورت می‌گیرد که ترامپ فشارها را بر ولودیمیر زلنسکی، رئیس‌جمهور اوکراین برای توقف هدف قرار دادن پالایشگاه‌های نفت روسیه تشدید کرده است، با این استدلال که این حملات باعث اختلال در عرضه جهانی گازوئیل شده و به افزایش قیمت سوخت برای مصرف‌کنندگان آمریکایی کمک کرده است. این موضوع با افزایش قیمت گازوئیل بر کشاورزان، کامیون داران و مشاغل آمریکایی به طور فزاینده ای ضروری شده است.
items.summary_original: President Donald Trump announced an immediate energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, saying both countries have agreed to halt attacks on each other's energy infrastructure after weeks of escalating tensions over strikes on oil refineries and power plants. "Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!" Trump wrote on Truth Social. The announcement comes as Trump has intensified pressure on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to stop targeting Russian oil refineries, arguing that the attacks have disrupted global diesel supplies and contributed to higher fuel prices for American consumers. The issue has become increasingly urgent as diesel prices weigh on American farmers, truckers and businesses that rely on the fuel to transport goods and operate heavy equipment. The announcement follows a contentious week in U.S.-Ukraine relations after Trump struck a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to allow Russian diesel exports to reach American and global markets. "Last night, radical protesters stormed the stage at our Lincoln Reagan Dinner and held up a KKK symbol while Speaker Lisa Demuth spoke," Plechash said in a statement posted to X by the Republican Party of Minnesota. Left leaning protesters aimed a symbol of racial terror at a Black woman leader, at a dinner named for the president who ended slavery," he continued. items.summary_original: Congress is scrambling to stop one of the United States' most iconic industries from fleeing overseas and taking thousands of jobs along with it. The U.S. TV and film industry has been hemorrhaging work for years as production companies and movie studios flee to places like Europe and Canada for friendlier tax regimes and other attractive financial policies. It prompted President Donald Trump to publicly call on Congress to pass legislation aimed at incentivizing entertainment studios to bring their production back home — and an unlikely alliance of lawmakers is heeding the call. A new bill that could potentially end up in a bipartisan tax package at the end of this year would push film and TV studios to bring their productions back to the U.S. via new tax incentives, with extra support if they choose to bring development to rural communities. items.summary_original: More than two decades after being elected to what was supposed to be a four-year term, Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas has once again postponed elections, extending a nearly 20-year wait for voters to choose a new legislature. Abbas issued a decree Friday pushing Palestinian Legislative Council elections from next month to Sept. 11, 2027, according to the official Palestinian news agency WAFA. Presidential elections , which have not been held since Abbas' 2005 victory, are also scheduled for that date. The delay allows Palestinian leaders to remain in power without facing voters and could further damage the credibility of the Palestinian Authority, which has faced criticism over corruption and its security cooperation with Israel. NICARAGUA'S ORTEGA SAYS COUNTRY WILL 'NEVER AGAIN' HOLD ELECTIONS, SHUTTING OUT OPPOSITION The Palestinian Authority, dominated by Abbas' Fatah party, governs parts of the West Bank under agreements reached in the 1990s. Palestinian officials cited conditions in the West Bank, Gaza Strip and east Jerusalem as reasons for postponing the vote. The Palestine Liberation Organization's Executive Committee, which Abbas heads, claimed Israel had blocked election materials and international observers from entering Gaza, according to The Associated Press. items.summary: ادوارد کوریستین، مهندس سابق DOGE که بیشتر به عنوان "توپ های بزرگ" شناخته می شود، اکنون به ساخت درب دیجیتالی جدید دولت ترامپ برای دولت فدرال کمک می کند - تلاشی با هدف ارائه یک مکان به آمریکایی ها برای پیمایش اطلاعات و در نهایت خدمات کامل اکنون در هزاران وب سایت دولتی پخش شده است. کوریستین در مصاحبه‌ای با فاکس نیوز دیجیتال گفت: «من فکر می‌کنم این واقعیت که ۲۹۰۰۰ وب‌سایت دولتی وجود دارد، بسیار دیوانه‌کننده است. "و هدف شهروندان این است که بفهمند از کدام وب سایت دولتی برای هر مورد خاص استفاده می کنند." کوریستین - که بیشتر در واشنگتن با نام مستعار "Big Balls" شناخته می شود - با فاکس نیوز دیجیتال در کاخ سفید در مورد نقش جدید خود در کمک به ساخت America.gov صحبت کرد.
items.summary_original: Edward Coristine, the former DOGE engineer better known as "Big Balls," is now helping build the Trump administration’s new digital front door to the federal government — an effort aimed at giving Americans one place to navigate information and, eventually, complete services now spread across thousands of government websites. "I think that the fact that there’s 29,000 government websites is pretty insane," Coristine told Fox News Digital in a sit-down interview. "And it is the citizens’ objective to have to go figure out which government website they’re supposed to use for each specific thing." Coristine — better known around Washington by his attention-grabbing "Big Balls" nickname — sat down with Fox News Digital at the White House to talk about his new role helping build America.gov , what he learned during his time at DOGE, the administration’s plans to make more government services fully digital, his experience being attacked in Washington, and how the nickname that helped make him famous actually came from his dad. TRUMP UNVEILS AMERICA.GOV AS AI-POWERED HUB FOR PASSPORTS, MEDICARE ENROLLMENT AND MORE Coristine is now working with the National Design Studio on the administration’s revamped America.gov , which launched Sept. 29 as an AI-powered single point of entry for information drawn from thousands of government websites. items.summary_original: Pope Leo XIV announced Sunday that he will undergo surgery to remove a small nodule from his lung, revealing the unexpected health concern to thousands of faithful gathered in St. Peter's Square following his traditional Angelus prayer. The 71-year-old pontiff said doctors discovered the nodule at a "very early stage" and recommended its removal. The surgery is scheduled for the coming days, with the pope expected to remain hospitalized for approximately one week, according to Vatican spokesman Matteo Bruni . "Doctors found a small lump in the lung," Leo said after the Angelus address. "It was identified at a very early stage and well situated." POPE LEO VISITS SITE OF MIRACLE CURES, MEETS PEOPLE WHOSE UNEXPLAINED HEALINGS STUNNED DOCTORS "The doctors consider it appropriate to intervene and so, following their advice, I decided to have surgery to remove it," he continued. "The surgery is already scheduled for the next few days. I thank you for your spiritual closeness and I rely on your prayer." The surgery is likely to take place within a few days at the Gemelli Hospital in Rome, which is known as the "Pope's" hospital, Vatican sources told Fox News. The Vatican has not disclosed whether the nodule is cancerous, and no further details about the pope's diagnosis or the planned procedure were immediately available. items.summary_original: Flock Safety, which operates controversial Flock cameras now in 49 states, is touting crime clearance rates in cities that use the cameras compared to cities that don't — as a nationwide battle over the surveillance tool rages. "It's used for any kind of crime really," Phil Arnold, a public affairs manager for the company, told Fox News Digital. "It's very helpful for hit-and-run accidents, also stolen vehicles, property crimes, crimes against people as well." Arnold is a retired law enforcement officer who served his community in Shorewood, Illinois, for 40 years. He was the chief police executive in the town for 27 years. FORMER PENTAGON AI CHIEF WARNS FLOCK CAMERAS COULD CREATE 'CHINA-LIKE SURVEILLANCE STATE' IN THE US Arnold told Fox News Digital that for the last seven years of his career, his department used automatic license plate reader (ALPR) technology, which Flock Safety operates, to help solve crimes, describing the innovation as nothing short of revolutionary. "Let me give you an example. Before we had this technology, someone would say, 'Hey, I just got robbed, and it was a white Chevy Tahoe,'" Arnold explained. "We would then put out this information, a BOLO [be on the lookout] so to speak, and police officers would stop every white Chevy Tahoe trying to find the offender." items.summary_original: In what it called a "Schools Decree," the Italian government announced last month that no student may cover their face in class, no classroom may exceed 30% foreign-born pupils and parents who skip mandatory Italian lessons could face fines of up to $1,120. The decree, which takes effect next summer, is framed as a push for "integration," but it raises the question of whether a Western democracy can force assimilation, or is it already too late? Nile Gardiner, director of The Heritage Foundation's Margaret Thatcher Center for Freedom said that it is "The single biggest issue of our time in Europe: Mass migration and Islamification." And had an ominous warning, "What you’re seeing in London and other European cities can easily happen in the U.S… These cultural shifts will all come to America, unless American leaders are willing to fight back." Italian Prime Minister Georgia Meloni defended the decree on X , calling the new rules "Tools of common sense that do not divide, but truly help to integrate, avoiding ghetto classes and giving all students the same opportunities. This is the direction we want to continue to follow: a school that integrates without giving up on rules, that supports those who have more difficulties and that puts everyone in a position to start from the same point." items.summary: به گفته الیوت کافمن، نویسنده سرمقاله وال استریت ژورنال و یک منبع دوم آشنا با دیلیبر، در حالی که اسرائیل آماده ترور رهبر حزب الله حسن نصرالله در سپتامبر 2024 بود، بنیامین نتانیاهو نخست وزیر و مقامات ارشد دفاعی وی در مورد اینکه آیا قبل از عملیات به دولت بایدن اطلاع داده شود یا خیر، اختلاف نظر داشتند، زیرا از ترس واشنگتن ممکن است این ماموریت را متوقف کند. به گفته کافمن، یکی از نویسندگان کتاب «در اتاق جنگ: داستان درونی نبرد اسرائیل علیه حماس و محور ایران» که این تبادل را در مصاحبه با فاکس نیوز دیجیتال بازگو کرد، نتانیاهو به مقامات ارشد دفاعی اسرائیل گفت: «140 درصد آنها این مأموریت را تأیید نمی‌کنند». یوآو گالانت، وزیر دفاع وقت، و هرزی هالوی، رئیس ستاد ارتش اسرائیل، بر این باور بودند که به واشنگتن اطلاع رسانی کردند.
items.summary_original: As Israel prepared to assassinate Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah in September 2024, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his senior defense officials disagreed over whether to notify the Biden administration ahead of the operation, fearing Washington could try to stop the mission, according to Wall Street Journal editorial writer Elliot Kaufman and a second source familiar with the deliberations. "140%, they won't approve of the mission," Netanyahu told senior Israeli defense officials, according to Kaufman, co-author of " In the War Room: The Inside Story of Israel's Fight Against Hamas and the Iranian Axis ," who recounted the exchange in an interview with Fox News Digital. Then-Defense Minister Yoav Gallant and IDF Chief of Staff Herzi Halevi favored informing Washington, believing the Americans might support a strike against a Hezbollah leader linked to the deaths of U.S. service members, according to Kaufman. Netanyahu, however, warned that then-U.S. National Security Adviser Jake Sullivan would "jump out of his skin" if he learned of the plans. The disagreement reflected a widening divide between Jerusalem and Washington over Israel's military campaign against Iran's regional proxies, as the Biden administration sought to prevent the fighting from escalating into a broader regional war. items.summary_original: The Justice Department has charged 64 foreign nationals across 17 states with unlawful voting, fraudulent voter registration and election-related offenses in roughly the last five weeks, according to figures provided to Fox News Digital, as federal prosecutors intensify election-integrity enforcement. Minnesota leads the nation with 11 defendants, followed by Pennsylvania with 10 and Texas with nine. Louisiana accounts for five, while New Jersey, California and Florida each have four, according to the department's latest tally. The nationwide crackdown comes as federal officials intensify scrutiny of voter-registration safeguards ahead of November's midterms, with recent elections underscoring how even a few illegal ballots can exceed the margin separating candidates . Fox News Digital mapped the states with the largest concentrations of defendants as DOJ says it has charged 104 people with voting fraud-related offenses since Trump returned to office in 2025. In Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, on Friday, anti-Israel demonstrators carried signs deploying emotionally charged language against Israel, including one featuring a Palestinian flag and a bloodied hand with the message, "STOP GENOCIDE." Nearby, two women carrying mock machine guns flanked a cardboard image of a handcuffed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu with a noose around his neck. items.summary_original: Student protests over crumbling schools despite billions in public spending are fueling a broader crisis in France, and experts warn that the country's mounting financial troubles, President Emmanuel Macron's weakened political center and radical movements are pushing the unrest far beyond its original educational grievances. Simone Rodan-Benzaquen, the Foundation for Defense of Democracies' senior envoy for Europe, told Fox News Digital in an interview from Paris that what began in September with legitimate complaints about school conditions has increasingly been exploited by political forces seeking confrontation with the state. "Overall, I'd say the anger is real, but the violence, I would say, is organized," she said, adding that destroying schools would do nothing to improve the education system. items.summary_original: A powerful 7.7 magnitude earthquake struck off Panama's southern coast Friday, shaking the country's capital as officials investigated a potential tsunami threat. The U.S. Geological Survey initially measured the earthquake at magnitude 8.0 before lowering its estimate to 7.7. The quake struck at 1:56 p.m. ET, at a depth of 7.8 miles, near Pitaloza Arriba, Panama. A 5.5 magnitude aftershock followed, with its epicenter approximately 50 miles east of the initial earthquake. The Panama Canal said operations were continuing normally following Friday's earthquake, with emergency protocols activated and technical teams inspecting facilities for possible damage. Canal officials said their priority was ensuring the safety of workers, vessels, crews and nearby communities as assessments continued. MORE THAN 3,000 MISSING AFTER COLOMBIA EARTHQUAKE AS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PROVIDES $15.5 MILLION IN RELIEF The earthquake was felt in Panama City and in San José, the capital of neighboring Costa Rica , according to Reuters. Tsunami officials warned that waves reaching 3 to 10 feet above tide levels were possible along some coastal areas of Panama, while parts of Ecuador could experience waves of approximately 1 to 3 feet. Smaller tsunami waves of less than 1 foot above tide levels were forecast for coastal areas of Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Mexico, Nicaragua and Peru. Dozens of protesters, most of them young and dressed in black with masks over their faces, were seen throwing rocks and firecrackers at police at the central Brussels railway station, The Associated Press reported. The chaos in the streets contributed to increased traffic across the Belgian capital. Police said the unrest was caused by people unaffiliated with the anti-austerity demonstration, which drew an estimated 30,000 participants, the AP reported. Two of Belgium’s largest labor unions organized Friday’s daylong national strike, with a separate public-sector walkout planned for Monday. items.summary_original: When young adults stormed France's Bastille on Thursday, a little-known media outlet called BreakThrough News sent followers a "BREAKING" alert: "French students flood Bastille Square in Paris." But that isn't the full story. A Fox News Digital investigation has found that a transnational network of far-left communist and socialist organizations is seizing on France’s fiery student protests to advance a wider political and ideological agenda, using tactics deployed in the United States over the past decade to amplify unrest, deepen divisions and project an image of chaos. Earlier in the week, BreakThrough News splashed another headline across the front of its website: "French students shut down schools in historic strike against austerity," mobilizing "with support from unions and progressive forces." But those "progressive forces" aren't limited to students demanding education reform as part of their "Lycéenne Mobilisation," or high school student mobilization. items.summary: به گزارش خبرگزاری رویترز، دو شهروند لتونیایی که به طور قانونی در بریتانیا زندگی می کنند، بر اساس بند 4 قانون امنیت ملی بریتانیا در سال 2023، روز پنجشنبه پس از ادعای نقض حصار محیطی در RAF Molesworth، یک پایگاه نظامی حساس بریتانیا که در آن عملیات اطلاعاتی مهم ایالات متحده و ناتو قرار دارد، دستگیر شدند. این دستگیری ها تحقیقات ضدتروریسم بزرگی را در مورد نقض امنیتی در تاسیسات استراتژیک، که به عنوان یک مرکز اطلاعاتی مرکزی از فرماندهان نظامی آمریکا در سراسر اروپا و آفریقا پشتیبانی می کند، آغاز کرد. بر اساس گزارش ها، این پایگاه همچنین تحت یک توسعه 556.5 میلیون دلاری بر روی مجتمع تحلیل اطلاعات مشترک (JIAC) قرار دارد، مکانی که برای ادغام 20 تاسیسات اطلاعاتی و گنجایش بیش از 1000 پرسنل طراحی شده است. ایران تحت نظارت
items.summary_original: Two Latvian nationals legally living in the United Kingdom were arrested under Section 4 of Britain's National Security Act of 2023 Thursday after allegedly breaching a perimeter fence at RAF Molesworth, a sensitive British military base housing critical U.S. and NATO intelligence operations, Reuters reported. The arrests triggered a major counterterrorism investigation into the security breach at the strategic installation, which serves as a central intelligence hub supporting American military commanders across Europe and Africa. The base is also undergoing a $556.5 million expansion centered on the Joint Intelligence Analysis Complex (JIAC), a location designed to consolidate 20 intelligence facilities and accommodate more than 1,000 personnel, according to reports . IRAN UNDER SCRUTINY AFTER PLOT FOILED NEAR UK BASE USED BY US MILITARY The suspects, ages 32 and 36, were discovered inside the base around 2 a.m. Thursday after an extensive security sweep. Ministry of Defense Police officers conducting routine patrols first raised the alarm around 10 p.m. Wednesday after finding an abandoned vehicle near the perimeter. Bomb disposal specialists cleared the vehicle before armed officers discovered a fence breach and located the men inside. Initially detained on suspicion of trespass and criminal damage, both men were arrested again under the National Security Act for allegedly entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the United Kingdom. They remain in custody

items.summary: مرگ یک زن 87 ساله که از خانه دیرینه اش بیرون رانده شده بود، بحران سیاسی در اسپانیا را تشدید کرده است، جایی که اعتراضات سراسری به دلیل افزایش هزینه های مسکن به برگزاری انتخابات زودهنگام کمک کرده است. به گزارش آسوشیتدپرس، ماریا دل کارمن آباسکال، معروف به "ماریکارمن" روز چهارشنبه پس از اخراج از آپارتمانی در مادرید که هفت دهه در آن زندگی می کرد، در بیمارستان بستری شد. مرگ او تنها چند روز پس از آن اتفاق افتاد که پدرو سانچز، نخست وزیر اسپانیا، پس از ناکامی دولتش در تصویب تدابیر اضطراری مسکن در پارلمان، انتخابات زودهنگام را برای 29 نوامبر فراخوان داد. این جنجال فشار جدیدی را بر حزب سوسیالیست سانچز وارد کرده است زیرا اسپانیا با ناامیدی گسترده از افزایش اجاره بها و قیمت مسکن دست و پنجه نرم می کند. تماس رهبر اپوزیسیون اسپانیا
items.summary_original: The death of an 87-year-old woman who was evicted from her longtime home has intensified a political crisis in Spain , where nationwide protests over soaring housing costs have helped force an early election. María del Carmen Abascal, known as "Maricarmen," died Wednesday after being hospitalized following her eviction from a Madrid apartment where she had lived for seven decades, according to The Associated Press. Her death came just days after Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called a snap election for Nov. 29 after his government's failure to pass emergency housing measures through Parliament. The controversy has put renewed pressure on Sánchez's Socialist Party as Spain grapples with widespread frustration over rising rents and housing affordability . SPANISH OPPOSITION LEADER CALLS PRIME MINISTER A ‘TRAITOR’ OVER CEUTA MIGRANT CRISIS At the center of the uproar was Abascal's Sept. 23 eviction, which drew national attention after images showed the elderly woman, who used a wheelchair, being carried from her apartment on a stretcher. Police had cordoned off the street and removed demonstrators who attempted to stop the eviction. The images sparked demonstrations in Madrid and other Spanish cities, turning Abascal into a symbol of the country's housing crisis. The real estate company responsible for her eviction had sought to lease the apartment at a substantially higher price, according to the AP. items.summary_original: An Iranian anti-regime protester was hanged at dawn Oct. 5 inside Isfahan Central Prison, just hours after marrying his imprisoned fiancée over a jail phone line, The Times reported Thursday. Alireza Sepahi, 25, was executed alongside co-defendant Alireza Raisi after being sentenced to death in the anti-government demonstrations at Isfahan’s Alikhani Square Jan. 8., according to Human Rights Iran . Sepahi and his bride, student activist Mahshad Keshani, 22, knew and loved each other before being arrested during anti-regime demonstrations, the report said. IRAN HANGS 2 PROTESTERS IN PUBLIC, CROWD CRIES 'DISHONORABLE' AS SECURITY FIRES TEAR GAS Keshani, who is serving a five-year sentence, pushed for an informal wedding Sunday as fears mounted that Sepahi’s execution was imminent after a final family summons. The couple exchanged vows over the phone from inside Isfahan prison, joined by their fathers. Human rights lawyer Amirsalar Davoudi facilitated the ceremony by reading the vows for the fathers to bless. Keshani’s family gave a copy of the Quran, a saffron rock candy and a single red rose as a traditional dowry. "It was Mahshad’s idea," Davoudi told The Times. "Even now, I wonder how one young woman can possess such courage." items.summary_original: The mother of Darya Shipilova, the 28-year-old Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and Far East worker whose death has sparked global public health concerns, pushed back against reports her daughter was infected after she broke a test tube. Svetlana Shipilova, who is a medical professional, told the Russian outlet Glubina she does not believe the account circulating regarding her daughter's demise, according to The Telegraph . "I know the truth," she reportedly said. "I’m having to fend off stupid acquaintances who believed all this. The clever ones didn’t believe it, of course. RUSSIAN BIO-LEAK SECRECY FOLLOWS CHERNOBYL PLAYBOOK, EX-CIA OFFICER WARNS "Not even all medical professionals understand it’s impossible to break a test tube like that," she added. "Even if you fling it at the wall. Only an amateur could say something like that. "Even hypothetically, you simply can’t spill what’s inside or break the tube. They’re that well protected." She also asserted to reporters, "They simply let my daughter die." items.summary: یک پسر 15 ساله با چاقو و دوربینی که روی کلاه ایمنی نصب شده بود به مدرسه ابتدایی لهستان که قبلاً در آن تحصیل می کرد حمله کرد و ظاهراً در دومین حمله با چاقو در مدرسه این کشور طی دو روز یک کارمند را کشت و دو نفر دیگر را زخمی کرد. مقامات در حال بررسی این موضوع هستند که آیا این حملات به یک چالش آنلاین مرتبط است که نوجوانان را تشویق می کند تا بیشترین تعداد ممکن را بکشند. پلیس گفت یک زن 37 ساله که به عنوان سرایدار کار می کرد در حمله صبح روز پنجشنبه در مدرسه در Leszczydol-Nowiny در شمال شرقی ورشو جان باخت. به گفته مقامات، کریستوف اوچمانسکی، معلم مدرسه، هنگام زیر سلطه گرفتن این نوجوان مجروح شد. اوچمانسکی به یک ایستگاه رادیویی گفت که صدای جیغی شنید و وارد راهرو شد. مادر متهم به تلاش برای کشتن دختران در تصادف آزادراه و حمله با چاقو در حالی که سربازان در قدم اول هستند
items.summary_original: A 15-year-old boy wielding a knife and wearing a helmet-mounted camera attacked a Polish primary school he used to attend, allegedly killing one employee and wounding two others in the country's second school stabbing in two days. Authorities are investigating whether the attacks are connected to an online challenge encouraging teenagers to kill as many people as possible. Police said a 37-year-old woman who worked as a caretaker died in the Thursday morning attack at the school in Leszczydol-Nowiny, northeast of Warsaw. The school's head teacher, Krzysztof Ochmanski, was injured while subduing the teenager, officials said. Ochmanski told a radio station he heard a scream and ran into a hallway. MOTHER ACCUSED OF TRYING TO KILL DAUGHTERS IN FREEWAY CRASH AND KNIFE ATTACK AS SOLDIERS STEP IN "He wounded me with the blade of a rather long knife — he had three knives on him — and hit me with the handle," Ochmanski told the public broadcaster Polskie Radio RDC. "By then, I had managed to restrain him." The day before the latest attack, a 19-year-old allegedly wounded 10 people, including himself, at a school in Ostroleka, which is in northeastern Poland. Also this week, police arrested a 17-year-old in Sierpc in north-central Poland after authorities suspected he was planning a similar attack, Reuters reported. items.title: بی‌طرفی، راستی‌آزمایی و پاسخ‌گویی؛ چرا بی‌بی‌سی فارسی بر این اصول ایستادگی می‌کند؟
items.summary: این مطلب توضیح می‌دهد که چرا بی‌بی‌سی فارسی در یکی از پرتنش‌ترین دوره‌های تاریخ معاصر ایران بر اصول بنیادین روزنامه‌نگاری، از جمله بی‌طرفی، راستی‌آزمایی، استقلال تحریریه و پاسخ‌گویی، پافشاری می‌کند. در این مقاله، با مرور شیوه تصمیم‌گیری‌های تحریریه، فرآیند راستی‌آزمایی اخبار، نحوه انتخاب مهمانان و برخورد با خطاها و انتقادها، تشریح می‌شود که هدف بی‌بی‌سی نه جانبداری از هیچ طرف، بلکه ارائه گزارشی دقیق، مستقل و مبتنی بر شواهد است تا مخاطبان بتوانند بر اساس اطلاعات قابل اعتماد، خود درباره رویدادها قضاوت کنند.

items.title: 'کودتای خزنده' در سپاه؛ نوار صوتی جلسه‌ای محرمانه در زمان جنگ
items.summary: با گذشت چهل سال از آغاز جنگ ایران و عراق، هنوز اطلاعات مرتبط با مقاطع مهمی از جنگ، از آرشیوهای محرمانه خارج نشده است. یکی از جلسات مهمی که در آن فرماندهی جنگ مورد انتقاد سپاهیان ناراضی قرار می‌گیرد، اوایل آذر ۶۳ برگزار می‌شود که در دهه‌های اخیر، رسانه‌های حکومتی ایران روایت‌های پراکنده و به‌شدت تحریف شده‌ای را از آن منتشر کرده‌اند.
